scenarios.name: pr-scan-github-actions-low-noise
scenarios.rationale: A has the zaproxy/action-baseline action with fail_action: true, a rules.tsv with tab-separated IGNORE for 10015, and allow_issue_writing: false, but it never grants issues: write; B covers fail_action, the rules file and issues: write, but it gives the rules file as a printf command rather than file content, hardcodes pr-123, and fails on any WARN, which works against 'only real issues'.

scenarios.name: staging-api-scan-with-reports
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses the right image and flags, gives chmod a+w, omits -S, warns to scan only systems the user owns or has permission to test, and gives the exit codes correctly (2 = warnings only). A adds -I, which suppresses the warning exit code and so weakens the exit-code explanation. A also gives a looser authorization warning and describes code 2 as 'at least one WARN'.

scenarios.name: authenticated-spa-automation-plan
scenarios.rationale: Both give an AF plan with env context, spiderAjax, browser authentication with autodetect verification, a report job, a docker zap.sh -cmd -autorun run, and credentials in env vars; A adds explicit exclude paths, an env-file, CI example, and a fallback to explicit verification (response/poll), making it somewhat more thorough, while B is more concise and its read -rs approach is nice but its verification and caveats are slightly thinner.
